Marie Tharp, who drew the first map of the entire ocean floor, sitting at her desk at Columbia University. NYC. 1956

Marie Tharp (1920 – 2006) was an American geologist and oceanographic cartographer who, in partnership with Bruce Heezen, created the first scientific map of the entire ocean floor. Their work revealed the presence of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, causing a paradigm shift in earth science that led to acceptance of the theories of plate tectonics and continental drift

In 1948 Tharp and Heezen met and their early work together used photographic data to locate downed aircraft from World War II. Later, they began to map the topography of the ocean floor. For the first 18 years of their collaboration, Heezen collected data aboard Columbia's ship, the Vema, and Tharp drew maps from that data, since women at that time still were excluded from working aboard ship. She was able to join data-collection expeditions in 1965. They published their map of the entire ocean floor in 1977.
